revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Studio Rental Formulas
revealWordProblem.text: Two producers at the music studio each wrote a formula for the cost, in dollars, of renting equipment for x hours. Producer A wrote 3x + 2x + 10. Producer B wrote 5x + 10. A client says the two producers are charging different amounts because the formulas look different. Is the client right? Show whether the two expressions are equivalent by simplifying Producer A's expression and combining like terms, and check your answer by substituting x = 6 into both expressions. What does each producer charge for a 6-hour rental?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The client is wrong — the expressions are equivalent. Simplify Producer A: 3x + 2x + 10 = 5x + 10, which matches Producer B exactly. Check x = 6: Producer A is 3(6) + 2(6) + 10 = 18 + 12 + 10 = 40, and Producer B is 5(6) + 10 = 40. Both producers charge $40 for a 6-hour rental.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that look different but have the same value for every allowed variable value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que se ven diferentes pero tienen el mismo valor para cada valor permitido de la variable.

vocabulary.definition: Expressions that always have the same value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Expresiones que siempre tienen el mismo valor.
vocabulary.visual: 2x + 4 and 2(x + 2): when x = 3, both = 10; when x = 7, both = 18 — always the same

vocabulary.definition: To write an expression in a shorter, simpler way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una expresión de forma más corta y simple.
vocabulary.visual: 3x + 2x + 5 simplifies to 5x + 5 — fewer terms, same value
vocabulary.cloze: To write an expression in its shortest equal form is to ___ it.

vocabulary.definition: Terms with the same letter raised to the same power, like 2x and 5x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Términos con la misma letra elevada a la misma potencia, como 2x y 5x.
vocabulary.visual: 3x and 7x are like terms (both x); 3x and 3y are NOT (x vs y); 3x and 3x² are NOT (x vs x²)
vocabulary.cloze: Terms with the same variable raised to the same power, like 4x and 9x, are ___.

examples.why: Both have the same variable x to the first power.
One has a variable and one does not, so they are not like terms.

vocabulary.definition: To add or subtract terms with the same letter into one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar o restar términos con la misma letra en uno solo.
vocabulary.visual: 4n + 3n = 7n — add the coefficients (4 + 3 = 7) and keep the variable (n)
vocabulary.cloze: To add or subtract like terms into one term is to ___ them.

vocabulary.definition: The number in front of a letter, like the 3 in 3x.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número frente a una letra, como el 3 en 3x.
vocabulary.visual: In 5x + 3, the coefficient of x is 5 — when x = 2, the 5x part equals 10
vocabulary.cloze: A number multiplied by a variable is a ___.

launch.narrative: At the music studio, two producers wrote formulas for the cost of renting equipment. Producer A wrote 3x + 2x + 10, and Producer B wrote 5x + 10. wonderPrompts: Can two expressions look completely different but always give the same answer?

conceptIntro.heading: When are two expressions equivalent?
conceptIntro.intro: Two expressions are equivalent when they always give the same value, no matter what number you put in for the variable. They can look different but mean the same thing.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Equivalent expressions give the same answer for every value of the variable.

optionalActivity.name: Equivalent Expression Match Battle
optionalActivity.intro: In the remix studio, two producers claim their beat formulas are the same — spin the tracks to prove which expressions are truly equivalent!

optional.stem: Producer A wrote 2(x + 3) for a beat's cost. Which expression is equivalent?
optional.explanation: Distribute the 2 to each term inside: 2 · x + 2 · 3 = 2x + 6. Check x = 5: 2(5 + 3) = 16 and 2(5) + 6 = 16.
choiceFeedback: The 2 reached the x but not the 3. Distributing means multiplying the outside factor by every term inside the parentheses.
Adding 2 + 3 first doesn't match the property. Distribute the 2.
Multiply 2 by x, and multiply 2 by 3, then add.
optional.stemEs: El productor A escribió 2(x + 3) para el costo de un beat. ¿Qué expresión es equivalente?
optional.explanationEs: Distribuye el 2 a cada término de adentro: 2 · x + 2 · 3 = 2x + 6. Comprueba con x = 5: 2(5 + 3) = 16 y 2(5) + 6 = 16.
hints: Two expressions are equivalent when they give the same value for every number you substitute.
The 2 outside the parentheses multiplies everything inside — that is the distributive property.
Start by multiplying 2 · x to get the first term, then do the same with the 3 inside and write the two results as a sum.
hintsEs: Dos expresiones son equivalentes cuando dan el mismo valor para cualquier número que sustituyas.
El 2 que está fuera del paréntesis multiplica a todo lo de adentro: esa es la propiedad distributiva.
Empieza multiplicando 2 · x para obtener el primer término, luego haz lo mismo con el 3 de adentro y escribe los dos resultados como una suma.

optional.stem: A track stacks 3x and then one more x. Which expression is equivalent to 3x + x?
optional.explanation: 3x + x is 3 groups of x plus 1 more group of x = 4x. Add the coefficients: 3 + 1 = 4. Check x = 3: 3(3) + 3 = 12 and 4(3) = 12.
choiceFeedback: 3x and x are like terms (same variable). 3x + x = 4x.
3x and x are different — x is the same as 1x, so 3x + 1x = 4x.
Combining like terms: 3 of something plus 1 more gives 4.
optional.stemEs: Una pista apila 3x y después una x más. ¿Qué expresión es equivalente a 3x + x?
optional.explanationEs: 3x + x son 3 grupos de x más 1 grupo más de x = 4x. Suma los coeficientes: 3 + 1 = 4. Comprueba con x = 3: 3(3) + 3 = 12 y 4(3) = 12.
hints: Like terms share the same variable, so they can be combined into a single term.
A lone x means 1x, so the second term already has a coefficient — it just is not written.
Rewrite the expression as 3x + 1x, then add the two coefficients to find the new coefficient of x.
hintsEs: Los términos semejantes comparten la misma variable, así que se pueden combinar en un solo término.
Una x sola significa 1x, así que el segundo término ya tiene coeficiente, solo que no está escrito.
Reescribe la expresión como 3x + 1x y luego suma los dos coeficientes para hallar el nuevo coeficiente de x.

optional.stem: Producer B flipped a formula to 5 + 2x. Which expression is equivalent?
optional.explanation: Order of addition does not change the value (commutative property): 5 + 2x = 2x + 5. Check x = 10: 5 + 2(10) = 25 and 2(10) + 5 = 25.
choiceFeedback: You added the 5 and the 2, but 5 is a constant and 2x has a variable. Only like terms can be combined.
This multiplies 5 by 2x, but the expression adds the two terms. Check the operation sign between them.
The 5 and the 2 traded places here, which changes the job each number does. In the original, the 2 is the coefficient attached to x.
optional.stemEs: El productor B cambió una fórmula a 5 + 2x. ¿Qué expresión es equivalente?
optional.explanationEs: El orden de la suma no cambia el valor (propiedad conmutativa): 5 + 2x = 2x + 5. Comprueba con x = 10: 5 + 2(10) = 25 y 2(10) + 5 = 25.
hints: Two expressions are equivalent when they always have the same value, even if the terms are written in a different order.
Addition can be done in either order, but each number has to stay attached to its own term.
Notice that 2x is one whole term and 5 is another. Try writing the two terms in the other order, keeping the 2 attached to the x, then test both versions with x = 10.
hintsEs: Dos expresiones son equivalentes cuando siempre tienen el mismo valor, aunque los términos estén escritos en otro orden.
La suma se puede hacer en cualquier orden, pero cada número debe quedarse unido a su propio término.
Fíjate en que 2x es un término completo y 5 es otro. Escribe los dos términos en el otro orden, dejando el 2 pegado a la x, y prueba las dos versiones con x = 10.

optional.instructions: The target beat formula is 4x + 6. Spin each expression onto the deck where it belongs: equivalent to 4x + 6, or NOT equivalent.
optional.explanation: Simplify each spin and compare it to 4x + 6. 2(2x + 3) distributes to 4x + 6; 4x + 3 + 3 combines the constants into 4x + 6; and x + x + x + x + 6 is four x's plus 6, which is 4x + 6. The other three miss: 4x + 10 has the wrong constant, 10x wrongly merges 4x and 6 into one term, and 4(x + 6) = 4x + 24 because the 4 must multiply the 6 too.
optional.explanationEs: Simplifica cada expresión y compárala con 4x + 6. 2(2x + 3) se distribuye y da 4x + 6; 4x + 3 + 3 combina las constantes y da 4x + 6; y x + x + x + x + 6 son cuatro x más 6, es decir 4x + 6. Las otras tres fallan: 4x + 10 tiene la constante equivocada, 10x junta mal 4x y 6 en un solo término, y 4(x + 6) = 4x + 24 porque el 4 también debe multiplicar al 6.
hints: Equivalent means it simplifies to exactly 4x + 6 — the x part AND the number part both have to match.
Simplify each card first: distribute anything in parentheses, combine like terms, then compare both pieces to 4x + 6.
Start with 2(2x + 3): multiply the 2 by BOTH terms inside, then check whether your result matches 4x + 6.
hintsEs: Ser equivalente significa que se simplifica exactamente a 4x + 6: tanto la parte con x COMO el número deben coincidir.
Primero simplifica cada tarjeta: distribuye lo que esté en paréntesis, combina términos semejantes y luego compara las dos partes con 4x + 6.
Empieza con 2(2x + 3): multiplica el 2 por LOS DOS términos de adentro y luego revisa si tu resultado coincide con 4x + 6.
optional.instructionsEs: La fórmula del ritmo objetivo es 4x + 6. Coloca cada expresión en la tornamesa que le corresponde: equivalente a 4x + 6, o NO equivalente.

optional.label: Match each studio beat formula to its equivalent remix.
optional.explanation: Each beat formula matches the remix with the same value. Distributing gives 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12 and 2(4a − 1) = 8a − 2. Combining like terms gives 7y + y = 8y and 9m − 3m = 6m. And 6 + 5n = 5n + 6, because addition can be written in either order without changing the value.
optional.explanationEs: Cada fórmula de ritmo se empareja con el remix que tiene el mismo valor. Distribuir da 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12 y 2(4a − 1) = 8a − 2. Combinar términos semejantes da 7y + y = 8y y 9m − 3m = 6m. Y 6 + 5n = 5n + 6, porque una suma se puede escribir en cualquier orden sin cambiar su valor.
hints: Every card on the left has one remix that means exactly the same thing — same variable term, same number.
Two tools cover all of these: distribute across parentheses, or combine like terms by adding and subtracting coefficients. One card only swaps the order of an addition.
Start with 3(x + 4): multiply the 3 by the x and by the 4, then look for the card that shows your result.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta de la izquierda tiene un remix que significa exactamente lo mismo: el mismo término con variable y el mismo número.
Dos herramientas bastan: distribuir en los paréntesis o combinar términos semejantes sumando y restando coeficientes. Una tarjeta solo cambia el orden de una suma.
Empieza con 3(x + 4): multiplica el 3 por la x y por el 4, y luego busca la tarjeta que muestra tu resultado.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — The False Remix

workedExample.label: Claim
workedExample.work: 2x and 6 are like terms, so combine them

optional.correctWork: 2x and 6 are NOT like terms — 2x has a variable and 6 is just a number, so they cannot be combined into one term. 2x + 6 is already simplified. You could rewrite it by factoring: 2x + 6 = 2(x + 3). Check x = 5: 2(5) + 6 = 16, but 8(5) = 40 — not equal, so 8x is wrong.
hints: Are 2x and 6 like terms? One has a variable and one does not.
Try substituting x = 5 into 2x + 6 and into 8x. Do you get the same value?
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: el remix falso
optional.explanation: 2x and 6 are NOT like terms — 2x carries a variable and 6 is just a number — so they cannot be merged into one term. 2x + 6 is already in simplest form; the only rewrite available is factoring: 2x + 6 = 2(x + 3). Testing x = 5 confirms it: 2(5) + 6 = 16, but 8(5) = 40.
optional.explanationEs: 2x y 6 NO son términos semejantes: 2x lleva una variable y 6 es solo un número, así que no se pueden unir en un solo término. 2x + 6 ya está en su forma más simple; lo único que se puede hacer es factorizar: 2x + 6 = 2(x + 3). Probar con x = 5 lo confirma: 2(5) + 6 = 16, pero 8(5) = 40.

choiceFeedback: 4x and 3x are like terms. 4x + 3x = 7x.
Combine like terms: 4 + 3 = 7, so 4x + 3x = 7x.
Both have the same variable x. Add the coefficients: 4 + 3 = 7.
hints: 4x and 3x share the exact same variable, x — that makes them like terms.
Combine like terms by adding the coefficients (the number parts). The variable tags along unchanged.
Add the coefficients: 4 + 3. Keep the x exactly as it is — no new exponent appears.
hintsEs: 4x y 3x comparten exactamente la misma variable, x: eso los hace términos semejantes.
Combina términos semejantes sumando los coeficientes (la parte numérica). La variable se queda igual.
Suma los coeficientes: 4 + 3. Conserva la x tal cual: no aparece ningún exponente nuevo.

choiceFeedback: You multiplied the 2 by the m but stopped there. The factor outside the parentheses has to reach every term inside.
Did you forget to distribute the 2 to both terms?
2 times m is 2m, and 2 times 5 is 10.
hints: The 2 outside the parentheses must multiply both the m and the 5.
Distribute: write 2 × m and 2 × 5, then join the products with +.
Start: 2 × m = 2m. Now multiply 2 × 5 and add that product on.
hintsEs: El 2 de afuera del paréntesis debe multiplicar tanto a la m como al 5.
Distribuye: escribe 2 × m y 2 × 5, y luego une los productos con +.
Empieza: 2 × m = 2m. Ahora multiplica 2 × 5 y agrega ese producto.

approaching.explanation: Multiplying 3 by each term inside the parentheses is the distributive property.
choiceFeedback: The commutative property changes the order of terms, like a + b = b + a. Look at what is happening to the 3 and the terms inside the parentheses instead.
That shows how multiplying across a sum works.
Distributing 3 to both x and 7 gives this pattern.
hints: Watch what happened to the 3: it multiplied the x AND the 7 across the parentheses.
The order didn't change and the grouping didn't just move — a factor was handed out to each term. Which property does that?
Check: 3 × x = 3x and 3 × 7 = 21 — both appear on the right. Name the property that multiplies across a sum.
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplicar el 3 por cada término dentro del paréntesis es la propiedad distributiva.
hintsEs: Fíjate en lo que le pasó al 3: multiplicó a la x Y al 7 a través del paréntesis.
El orden no cambió y la agrupación no solo se movió: se repartió un factor a cada término. ¿Qué propiedad hace eso?
Comprueba: 3 × x = 3x y 3 × 7 = 21, y ambos aparecen a la derecha. Nombra la propiedad que multiplica a través de una suma.

approaching.explanation: 5n + 2n = 7n. Add the coefficients: 5 + 2 = 7. The variable stays as n.
choiceFeedback: 5n and 2n are like terms. 5n + 2n = 7n.
Combine: 5 + 2 = 7, so 5n + 2n = 7n.
Both terms have n. Add the coefficients: 5 + 2.
hints: 5n and 2n both have the variable n — they're like terms, so they can combine.
Add the number parts (coefficients) and keep n the same. Don't multiply them.
Compute 5 + 2 for the new coefficient, then write it in front of n.
approaching.explanationEs: 5n + 2n = 7n. Suma los coeficientes: 5 + 2 = 7. La variable sigue siendo n.
hintsEs: 5n y 2n tienen ambos la variable n: son términos semejantes, así que se pueden combinar.
Suma las partes numéricas (coeficientes) y conserva n igual. No los multipliques.
Calcula 5 + 2 para el coeficiente nuevo y luego escríbelo delante de n.

approaching.instructions: Sort each pair of expressions by whether they are equivalent or not.
hints: Equivalent means always equal. Simplify the first expression in each pair and compare with the second.
Combine like terms or distribute — and remember, a plain number like 3 can't join a variable term like 4a.
First card: does 3x + 2x really simplify to 5x? Add the coefficients to check, then place the card.
approaching.explanation: Simplify the first expression on each card and see whether it matches the second. 3x + 2x = 5x, 2(n + 4) = 2n + 8, and x + x = 2x, so those three pairs are equivalent. 4a + 3 and 3y + 2 cannot be combined at all, because a plain number is not a like term with a variable term — so 4a + 3 is not 7a and 3y + 2 is not 5y.
approaching.explanationEs: Simplifica la primera expresión de cada tarjeta y revisa si coincide con la segunda. 3x + 2x = 5x, 2(n + 4) = 2n + 8 y x + x = 2x, así que esos tres pares son equivalentes. 4a + 3 y 3y + 2 no se pueden combinar, porque un número solo no es un término semejante de un término con variable: por eso 4a + 3 no es 7a y 3y + 2 no es 5y.
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada pareja de expresiones según si son equivalentes o no.
hintsEs: Equivalente significa siempre igual. Simplifica la primera expresión de cada pareja y compárala con la segunda.
Combina términos semejantes o distribuye, y recuerda que un número simple como 3 no se junta con un término variable como 4a.
Primera tarjeta: ¿de verdad 3x + 2x se simplifica a 5x? Suma los coeficientes para revisarlo y luego coloca la tarjeta.

approaching.title: Spot the Distributive Mistake

workedExample.label: Distribute
workedExample.work: Multiply the 3 by the first term only: 3 · x + 4

approaching.correctWork: The 3 must multiply BOTH terms inside the parentheses, not just the first one: 3 · x + 3 · 4 = 3x + 12. Check x = 2: 3(2 + 4) = 18 and 3(2) + 12 = 18, but 3(2) + 4 = 10 — so 3x + 4 is wrong.
hints: How many terms are inside the parentheses? The 3 multiplies each one.
Substitute x = 2 into 3(x + 4) and into 3x + 4. Do you get the same value?
approaching.titleEs: Detecta el error con la propiedad distributiva
approaching.explanation: The 3 sits outside parentheses that hold two terms, so it must multiply BOTH of them: 3 · x + 3 · 4 = 3x + 12. Multiplying only the x leaves the 4 untouched. Testing x = 2 shows the difference: 3(2 + 4) = 18 and 3(2) + 12 = 18, but 3(2) + 4 = 10.
approaching.explanationEs: El 3 está fuera de un paréntesis que contiene dos términos, así que debe multiplicar a LOS DOS: 3 · x + 3 · 4 = 3x + 12. Multiplicar solo la x deja el 4 sin tocar. Probar con x = 2 muestra la diferencia: 3(2 + 4) = 18 y 3(2) + 12 = 18, pero 3(2) + 4 = 10.

onLevel.instructions: Match each expression with its simplified form.
hints: Each card claims an expression simplifies to the given form. Verify the claim before placing it.
Redo the work yourself: combine like terms or distribute, and check both the variable part and the constant.
First card: 8y + 2y — add the coefficients 8 + 2 and see whether the result matches the card's 10y.
onLevel.explanation: Every card on this deck checks out. 8y + 2y = 10y and 6t + t = 7t come from adding coefficients, 9p − 3p = 6p from subtracting them, and 5n + 4 + 2n = 7n + 4 combines only the n terms while the 4 stays put. The other two come from distributing to BOTH terms inside the parentheses: 3(a + 6) = 3a + 18 and 4(2x − 1) = 8x − 4.
onLevel.explanationEs: Todas las tarjetas de este grupo son correctas. 8y + 2y = 10y y 6t + t = 7t salen de sumar coeficientes, 9p − 3p = 6p de restarlos, y 5n + 4 + 2n = 7n + 4 combina solo los términos con n mientras el 4 se queda igual. Las otras dos salen de distribuir a LOS DOS términos del paréntesis: 3(a + 6) = 3a + 18 y 4(2x − 1) = 8x − 4.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Une cada expresión con su forma simplificada.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta afirma que una expresión se simplifica a la forma dada. Verifica la afirmación antes de colocarla.
Rehaz el trabajo tú mismo: combina términos semejantes o distribuye, y revisa tanto la parte variable como la constante.
Primera tarjeta: 8y + 2y — suma los coeficientes 8 + 2 y mira si el resultado coincide con el 10y de la tarjeta.

onLevel.label: Match each expression to its simplified equivalent.
hints: Each left card simplifies to exactly one right card. Simplify first, then hunt for the result.
Two tools: combine like terms (add coefficients) or distribute a factor across parentheses. Constants stay separate.
Start with 6x + 2x: add 6 + 2 to get the coefficient, then find the card with that many x's.
onLevel.explanation: Each expression on the left simplifies to exactly one card on the right. Combining like terms gives 6x + 2x = 8x, 4a + 7 + a = 5a + 7, and 10m − 4m + 1 = 6m + 1. Distributing gives 3(n + 5) = 3n + 15, 2(3y − 4) = 6y − 8, and 5(x + 2) = 5x + 10, since the outside factor multiplies both terms inside.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada expresión de la izquierda se simplifica exactamente a una tarjeta de la derecha. Combinar términos semejantes da 6x + 2x = 8x, 4a + 7 + a = 5a + 7 y 10m − 4m + 1 = 6m + 1. Distribuir da 3(n + 5) = 3n + 15, 2(3y − 4) = 6y − 8 y 5(x + 2) = 5x + 10, porque el factor de afuera multiplica a los dos términos de adentro.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada expresión con su equivalente simplificado.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta de la izquierda se simplifica a exactamente una de la derecha. Simplifica primero y luego busca el resultado.
Dos herramientas: combinar términos semejantes (sumar coeficientes) o distribuir un factor por el paréntesis. Las constantes van aparte.
Empieza con 6x + 2x: suma 6 + 2 para obtener el coeficiente y luego busca la tarjeta con esa cantidad de x.

onLevel.instructions: Simplify each expression. Then evaluate both the original and simplified form when x = 3 to verify they are equivalent.
hints: Each row has two jobs: simplify the expression, then plug in x = 3 to check your simplified form.
Combine like terms or distribute first. Then substitute 3 into your simplified version and compute.
Row 1: 2x + 5x + 1 — combine 2x + 5x first and keep the + 1. Then replace x with 3 and evaluate.
onLevel.explanation: Simplify first, then substitute to check. 2x + 5x + 1 = 7x + 1, and at x = 3 that is 21 + 1 = 22. 4(x + 2) = 4x + 8, and at x = 3 that is 12 + 8 = 20. 3x + 4 + x − 1 = 4x + 3, and at x = 3 that is 12 + 3 = 15. Each simplified form gives the same value as the original, which is exactly what equivalent means.
onLevel.explanationEs: Primero simplifica y luego sustituye para comprobar. 2x + 5x + 1 = 7x + 1, y en x = 3 eso es 21 + 1 = 22. 4(x + 2) = 4x + 8, y en x = 3 eso es 12 + 8 = 20. 3x + 4 + x − 1 = 4x + 3, y en x = 3 eso es 12 + 3 = 15. Cada forma simplificada da el mismo valor que la original, que es justo lo que significa ser equivalentes.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Simplifica cada expresión. Después evalúa la forma original y la simplificada cuando x = 3 para comprobar que son equivalentes.
hintsEs: Cada fila tiene dos tareas: simplificar la expresión y luego sustituir x = 3 para comprobar tu forma simplificada.
Combina términos semejantes o distribuye primero. Luego sustituye 3 en tu versión simplificada y calcula.
Fila 1: 2x + 5x + 1 — combina primero 2x + 5x y conserva el + 1. Luego reemplaza x por 3 y evalúa.

onLevel.instructions: Are these equivalent? Test with x = 2. Left: 3x + 2x + 4. Right: 5x + 4.
onLevel.label: Both equal 14 — they are equivalent because 3x + 2x = 5x.
onLevel.hint: Combine like terms by adding or subtracting the coefficients while keeping the variable.
hints: The question is whether 3x + 2x + 4 always equals 5x + 4. Testing x = 2 gives you evidence.
Substitute 2 for every x on both sides, multiply first, then add. Compare the two totals.
Left: 3(2) + 2(2) + 4. Multiply each piece, add them up, then evaluate the right side and compare.
onLevel.explanation: Substituting x = 2 gives 3(2) + 2(2) + 4 = 6 + 4 + 4 = 14 on the left and 5(2) + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14 on the right, so the scale balances. It balances for every value of x, not just 2, because 3x + 2x combines to 5x — the two sides are the same expression written two ways.
onLevel.explanationEs: Al sustituir x = 2 se obtiene 3(2) + 2(2) + 4 = 6 + 4 + 4 = 14 del lado izquierdo y 5(2) + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14 del lado derecho, así que la balanza queda equilibrada. Se equilibra con cualquier valor de x, no solo con 2, porque 3x + 2x se combina en 5x: los dos lados son la misma expresión escrita de dos formas.

onLevel.title: Spot the Combining Mistake

workedExample.label: Combine
workedExample.work: Combine every number you see: 7x + 2x + 3 = 9x + 3, then add the 9 and 3 too

onLevel.correctWork: Only LIKE terms combine. 7x and 2x are like terms (7x + 2x = 9x), but the 3 is a constant and cannot be added to the 9x. The simplified form is 9x + 3. Check x = 2: 7(2) + 3 + 2(2) = 21 and 9(2) + 3 = 21, but 12(2) = 24 — so 12x is wrong.
hints: Can you add 9x and 3 into one term? Are they like terms?
Substitute x = 2 into 7x + 3 + 2x and into 12x. Do you get the same value?
onLevel.titleEs: Detecta el error al combinar términos
onLevel.explanation: 7x and 2x are like terms, so 7x + 2x = 9x is fine — but the step keeps going and adds the 9 to the 3. A constant like 3 has no variable, so it cannot join 9x in one term. The simplified form is 9x + 3. Check with x = 2: 7(2) + 3 + 2(2) = 21 and 9(2) + 3 = 21, but 12(2) = 24.
onLevel.explanationEs: 7x y 2x son términos semejantes, así que 7x + 2x = 9x está bien, pero el paso sigue y suma el 9 con el 3. Una constante como 3 no tiene variable, así que no puede unirse con 9x en un solo término. La forma simplificada es 9x + 3. Comprueba con x = 2: 7(2) + 3 + 2(2) = 21 y 9(2) + 3 = 21, pero 12(2) = 24.

extending.title: Find the Simplification Error
extending.correctWork: 3x + 2x = 5x (NOT 5x²). When you combine like terms, you add the coefficients, not multiply them. The correct answer is 5x + 6.
hints: When you combine 3x + 2x, do you add the exponents or the coefficients?
3x means 3 groups of x. 2x means 2 groups of x. Together that's ___ groups of x.
extending.explanation: Rearranging to 3x + 2x + 5 + 1 is correct. The error is in the last step: combining like terms adds the COEFFICIENTS, so 3x + 2x = 5x, not 5x². The exponent never changes when you add like terms, so the answer is 5x + 6.
extending.explanationEs: Reacomodar a 3x + 2x + 5 + 1 está correcto. El error está en el último paso: combinar términos semejantes suma los COEFICIENTES, así que 3x + 2x = 5x, no 5x². El exponente no cambia nunca al sumar términos semejantes, así que la respuesta es 5x + 6.

extending.prompt: A student says 2x + 3 and 5x are equivalent because both equal 5 when x = 1. Is the student correct? Explain why testing one value is not enough to prove equivalence, and find a value of x where they give different results.
extending.sentenceFrame: The student is ___ because ___. When x = 1: 2(1) + 3 = ___ and 5(1) = ___. But when x = ___: 2(___) + 3 = ___ and 5(___) = ___. To prove equivalence, expressions must be equal for ___ values of x.
extending.hint: Look for expressions that are equivalent by using properties like Commutative (rearrange) or Distributive (expand/factor).
hints: Both expressions equal 5 at x = 1 — but equivalence means equal for EVERY value of x.
Hunt for a counterexample: pick another value, like x = 2, and evaluate both expressions.
Try x = 2: compute 2(2) + 3 and 5(2). If the results differ, you've proven they're not equivalent.
extending.explanation: The student is not correct. Both expressions really do equal 5 when x = 1, but equivalence means equal for EVERY value of x, and one lucky match proves nothing. Testing x = 2 gives 2(2) + 3 = 7 while 5(2) = 10 — that single counterexample settles it.
extending.explanationEs: El estudiante no tiene razón. Las dos expresiones sí valen 5 cuando x = 1, pero ser equivalentes significa ser iguales para TODOS los valores de x, y una coincidencia de suerte no prueba nada. Al probar x = 2 se obtiene 2(2) + 3 = 7 mientras que 5(2) = 10; ese solo contraejemplo lo resuelve.
extending.promptEs: Un estudiante dice que 2x + 3 y 5x son equivalentes porque las dos dan 5 cuando x = 1. ¿Tiene razón? Explica por qué probar un solo valor no basta para demostrar equivalencia y encuentra un valor de x donde den resultados diferentes.
hintsEs: Ambas expresiones dan 5 cuando x = 1, pero equivalencia significa ser iguales para CADA valor de x.
Busca un contraejemplo: escoge otro valor, como x = 2, y evalúa ambas expresiones.
Prueba x = 2: calcula 2(2) + 3 y 5(2). Si los resultados son distintos, probaste que no son equivalentes.

extending.instructions: For each expression, find an equivalent expression using a DIFFERENT method (distributive property, combining like terms, or factoring).
hints: Each row wants a DIFFERENT-looking but equal expression. Your tools: factor, combine like terms, or distribute.
If it has parentheses, distribute. If terms repeat a variable, combine them. If terms share a factor, factor it out.
Row 1: 4x + 8 — both terms divide by 4. Pull that 4 outside parentheses and write what's left inside.
extending.explanation: Each row asks for a different-looking but equal form. 4x + 8 has terms that share a factor of 4, so factor it: 4(x + 2). 3a + 2a + 5 has like terms to combine: 5a + 5. And 6(n − 2) has parentheses to distribute: 6n − 12. All three moves change how the expression looks without changing its value.
extending.explanationEs: Cada fila pide una forma distinta pero igual en valor. 4x + 8 tiene términos que comparten el factor 4, así que factorízalo: 4(x + 2). 3a + 2a + 5 tiene términos semejantes que se combinan: 5a + 5. Y 6(n − 2) tiene un paréntesis para distribuir: 6n − 12. Los tres movimientos cambian cómo se ve la expresión sin cambiar su valor.
extending.instructionsEs: Para cada expresión, encuentra una expresión equivalente usando un método DIFERENTE (propiedad distributiva, combinar términos semejantes o factorizar).
hintsEs: Cada fila quiere una expresión de aspecto DIFERENTE pero igual. Tus herramientas: factorizar, combinar términos semejantes o distribuir.
Si tiene paréntesis, distribuye. Si hay términos que repiten una variable, combínalos. Si los términos comparten un factor, sácalo.
Fila 1: 4x + 8 — ambos términos se dividen entre 4. Saca ese 4 fuera del paréntesis y escribe lo que queda adentro.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Equivalent Expressions is adding the exponents instead of the coefficients when combining like terms — writing 3x + 2x as 5x² instead of 5x. Remember: 3x means 3 groups of x and 2x means 2 more groups of x, so you add the coefficients (3 + 2 = 5) and keep the variable's power the same (x¹, not x²).

diagram.title: Two Fair Studio Prices
diagram.caption: Both bars are the same length: Client A's 4h and 2h combine to 6h, and both add 30 — so 4h + 2h + 30 equals 6h + 30.

connect.scenario: A music studio charges different clients using different formulas. Client A pays 4h + 2h + 30 for h hours. Client B pays 6h + 30. A new client asks if the pricing is fair.
connect.promptQuestion: Are these expressions equivalent? How can you prove it?
connect.prompt: The expressions ___ equivalent because when I simplify 4h + 2h + 30, I get ___. I can prove it by substituting h = ___: both expressions equal ___.

check.explanation: 4h and 2h are like terms: 4h + 2h = 6h. The 30 has no h, so it stays separate.

check.stem: Are the two pricing formulas equivalent?
check.explanation: They simplify to the same expression, so both clients pay the same for any number of hours. The pricing is fair.

check.stem: Test it: what does each expression equal when h = 5?

connect.modelAnswer: The expressions ARE equivalent. Combining like terms, 4h + 2h + 30 = 6h + 30 — exactly Client B's formula. Substituting a value proves it: at h = 5, Client A pays 20 + 10 + 30 = 60 and Client B pays 30 + 30 = 60. The pricing is fair.

exitTicket.explanation: 6n + 3n = 9n and 4 − 1 = 3, so the simplified expression is 9n + 3.
choiceFeedback: 3x + 2x = 5x (combine like terms). 3 + 5 = 8. Together: 5x + 8.
Did you combine 3 + 2 + x? Remember: 3x + 2x = 5x, then add 8.
Like terms first: 3x + 2x = 5x. Then add the constant 8.
hints: Sort the terms into two families: n-terms (6n, 3n) and plain numbers (4, −1).
Combine each family separately — add the n coefficients, then handle 4 − 1. Never mix the families.
Start with the n-terms: 6n + 3n. Add those coefficients, then combine 4 − 1 for the constant part.

questions.explanation: The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. You multiply the outside factor by EACH term inside the parentheses.
